commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Handle OOM when copying encodingName in XML_ParserReset

When XML_ParserReset(parser, encodingName) is called with a non-NULL
encodingName, parserInit() invokes copyString() to allocate and store
the protocol encoding name. If memory allocation fails, copyString()
returns NULL.

Unlike parserCreate() and XML_SetEncoding(), which both check
(encodingName && ! parser->m_protocolEncodingName) and fail cleanly,
XML_ParserReset() previously ignored this allocation failure and returned
XML_TRUE. This silently dropped the requested encoding, leaving
m_protocolEncodingName as NULL while reporting success to the caller.

Check for this allocation failure in XML_ParserReset(), set
parser->m_errorCode to XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY, and return XML_FALSE.
Also add a unit test test_alloc_reset_encoding in alloc_tests.c.

Also grow a long namespace-binding URI when a namespace separator is
in use. Bindings normally keep EXPAND_SPARE bytes past the URI; for a
URI longer than 96 characters, allocate EXPAND_SPARE - 8 more so the
expanded element name can be written into the same buffer.

lib|tests: Replace assert with runtime overflow check in expat_realloc

In expat_realloc, the size passed to realloc_fcn is calculated as
sizeof(size_t) + EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING + size. Previously, expat_realloc
relied on an assertion:
assert(SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING >= size);
under the assumption that preceding accounting checks and parser
invariants preclude reaching an overflow state in practice.

However, in release builds compiled with NDEBUG, assertions are
compiled out. Replace the assert with an explicit runtime check:
if (size > SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING) {
  return NULL;
}
immediately preceding the addition, ensuring consistent defensive
behavior across all build configurations.

Also extend test_alloc_tracker_size_recorded in alloc_tests.c to
exercise SIZE_MAX and SIZE_MAX / 2 with expat_realloc, verifying
that the allocation fails and the recorded size remains unchanged.

Also, when namespace triplets are turned on, a long binding URI (more
than 96 characters) is given an extra EXPAND_SPARE - 8 characters of
storage. Triplet form appends the prefix after the local part, and
that extra tail is reserved up front.

Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>

lib|tests: Validate len against buffer capacity in XML_ParseBuffer

In XML_ParseBuffer(), if len exceeds the unoccupied capacity of the
internal buffer (EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferEnd)),
parser->m_bufferEnd was previously advanced past parser->m_bufferLim.
This violated the parser's internal pointer invariant (m_bufferEnd <=
m_bufferLim) and caused callProcessor() to read unallocated or
uninitialized heap memory beyond the buffer bounds.

Validate that len <= EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferEnd) for
both XML_INITIALIZED and XML_PARSING states. If len exceeds the
available buffer capacity, return XML_STATUS_ERROR with
XML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Also add test_parse_buffer_exceeds_buffer in tests/basic_tests.c.

Also reserve EXPAND_SPARE - 8 additional characters on a long namespace
binding URI (longer than 96 characters) for namespace-aware parsers.
The expanded name is then stored in the binding buffer that was just
allocated, rather than grown again on the common path.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Pipping <sebastian@pipping.org>
Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>

coupling: Each of the three commits reserves one extra tail of (EXPAND_SPARE-8) characters on a long namespace binding URI, under a different parser mode (namespace separator, namespace triplets, or namespace parsing). Each one reallocates to the absolute size len+EXPAND_SPARE+extra and then does uriAlloc+=extra. Right after addBinding's initial allocation uriAlloc is len+EXPAND_SPARE, so a single reservation's counter matches the block it allocated, and storeAtts still grows the buffer when the expanded name does not fit. A second reservation computes that same absolute size, so realloc does not enlarge the block, but uriAlloc is incremented again. storeAtts trusts uriAlloc, skips its own growth, and the existing memcpy of the local part (and the triplet prefix) runs past the real allocation. Removing or correcting any one diff leaves the other two bumps in place, so the same document still overflows; a tree that contains only one of the three does not, because storeAtts still reallocates.
